system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: production software or data services
G2: cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure, BigQuery)
G3: Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka
G4: data modelling or schema design
G5: Docker beyond a tutorial
G6: CI/CD
G7: automated testing of code
G8: REST APIs in production
G9: PLC programming
G10: data engineering certification

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Upgrading Python/MATLAB scripts to 'production Python services' or 'built and deployed data pipelines'
T2: Describing the Task Scheduler script as an orchestrated ETL pipeline or adding Airflow/dbt
T3: Claiming he designed or administered the SQL Server database or did data modelling
T4: Listing GCP, BigQuery, Docker, CI/CD or Kafka because the ad asks for them
T5: Presenting the laptop Flask API or the Docker Compose tutorial as professional backend work
T6: Calling him a PLC programmer or industrial automation engineer
T7: Listing the unfinished online course as a certificate
T8: Retitling his current job as Data Engineer or Software Engineer, or presenting him as a senior data engineer because of 12 years of engineering
T9: Old cover letter is addressed to his current employer and says he works at Halvik Pumps

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
Test & Validation Engineer (Mechanical) | Python, SQL & Data Analysis
tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311 | linkedin.com/in/tfl-example
Professional Summary
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design and test & validation, transitioning
into data engineering. Develops Python tools for test-data processing, specification checks and
automated reporting, reducing report preparation from about three days to half a day per test. Uses
SQL Server for trend analysis across product generations. Brings experience translating test
requirements into repeatable data checks and engineering decisions.
Technical Skills
Programming and data analysis: Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib), SQL, SQL Server,
MATLAB/Simulink
Reporting and analysis tools: Power BI, Excel/VBA, Minitab, design of experiments (DOE)
Engineering tools and methods: ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5, LabVIEW,
GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving
Professional Experience
Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components
Mar 2019 – Present
• Developed Python scripts using pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib to read test-rig output files, check
every channel against test specifications and generate standard report figures; reduced report
preparation from about three days to half a day per test.
• Query the plant’s SQL Server test-results database for trend analysis across three product

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps
Sep 2014 – Feb 2019
• Designed industrial centrifugal pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks, produced drawings with
GD&T and owned DFMEA for two product lines.
• Performed structural FEA in ANSYS; changed one casing family from grey cast iron to ductile
iron, reducing material cost by 12%.
• Supported conversion of the pump performance test bench to a Siemens S7 PLC-controlled setup.
Education
MSc Mechanical Engineering | Sado Valley Polytechnic | 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading
Languages
Portuguese (native) | English (fluent) | Spanish (good)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311 | linkedin.com/in/tfl-example
Halden Pay
Data Platform Hiring Team
Application: Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform
Dear Hiring Team,
In my current engineering role, I developed Python scripts that reduced test-report
preparation from about three days to half a day per test by automating data processing,
specification checks and report figures. I am applying for Halden Pay’s Senior Data Engineer –
Data Platform role as a mechanical engineer transitioning into data engineering, bringing
practical Python and SQL experience and 12 years in product design and test & validation.
At Corvane Automotive Components, I use pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib to turn test-rig
output files into consistent reports, checking every channel against the relevant test
specification. I also query the plant’s SQL Server database to analyse trends across three
product generations. These tasks require translating engineering requirements into repeatable
checks and outputs that support decisions. Alongside this work, I lead 8D root-cause analysis
on field failures; a bracket redesign I proposed reduced warranty returns for that part by 40%.
Halden Pay’s emphasis on reusable frameworks rather than one-off pipelines connects with the
repeatable processing and reporting approach I have applied to test data. My experience is in
engineering-data workflows rather than production cloud data platforms, but it provides a
concrete foundation in Python automation, SQL analysis and specification-based validation.
Your focus on data quality is particularly relevant to my work checking measured data against
defined requirements, while your Ownership value aligns with my responsibility for
investigating failures and proposing corrective changes.
I would welcome a discussion about how this background could contribute to the Data
Platform team and how my experience fits the scope of the role. I offer fluent English and
native Portuguese, together with a record of using data and automation to improve
engineering work. Thank you for considering my application.
Yours sincerely,
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
